definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection consisting of a flat rice cake filled with sweet bean paste and wrapped in an oak leaf. Eaten during Children's Day (May 5).

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{日|ひ}に{柏餅|かしわもち}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat kashiwa mochi on Children's Day.

examples.japanese: {和菓子屋|わがしや}で{柏餅|かしわもち}を{買|か}ってきた。
examples.english: I bought kashiwa mochi from a Japanese confectionery shop.

examples.japanese: {柏|かしわ}の{葉|は}は{新芽|しんめ}が{出|で}るまで{落|お}ちないので、{柏餅|かしわもち}は{子孫|しそん}{繁栄|はんえい}の{縁起物|えんぎもの}とされている。
examples.english: Because oak leaves don't fall until new buds appear, kashiwa mochi is considered a good-luck charm for the prosperity of one's descendants.

notes:
A seasonal Japanese sweet closely associated with {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day / Children's Day, May 5). The oak leaf ({柏|かしわ}の{葉|は}) wrapping is symbolic: because oak trees hold their old leaves until new growth appears, the leaf represents the continuity of family lineage.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally eaten on May 5th as part of Children's Day celebrations. The filling is typically {餡子|あんこ} (sweet red bean paste), though {味噌餡|みそあん} (sweet miso paste) is also common. The leaf is not eaten — it serves as a wrapper and imparts a subtle aroma.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {柏餅|かしわもち}を{食|た}べる — to eat kashiwa mochi
- {柏餅|かしわもち}を{作|つく}る — to make kashiwa mochi
- こし{餡|あん}の{柏餅|かしわもち} — kashiwa mochi with smooth bean paste

RELATED WORDS:
- {鏡餅|かがみもち} — New Year's rice cake offering; a different seasonal mochi
- {桜餅|さくらもち} — cherry blossom rice cake; a spring sweet wrapped in a cherry leaf
- {粽|ちまき} — rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaves; also eaten on May 5th
